items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: EU AI Act Gives Publishers Leverage, but No Teeth
items.excerpt: A Frankfurt panel on trust in science in the age of AI concluded that the EU AI Act helps rights holders on paper, but it has no penalties for AI developers and gives researchers no incentives.

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: Audible-Commissioned Survey Finds Audio Sends Readers Back to Print; Half Would Try AI Narration
items.excerpt: A NielsenIQ survey for Audible across 11 markets finds that audiobooks lead listeners back to print and e-books, and that about half of respondents would try AI narration, with more interest for fiction. Audible has not detailed the methodology.

history_match.title: Spotify's AI-powered audiobook narration opens up to all authors

items.title: Frankfurter Buchmesse 2026: ENLIT Network Provides Support for European Literary Translation and Translators
items.excerpt: European translation-funding bodies say literary translators currently have strong support, but AI makes their position fragile. Speakers framed AI as a dictionary-like tool that still cannot handle humor, emotion or voice.

history_match.title: Lost in Translation: AI comes for literary translators

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Publishing Jobs Will Adapt to AI, Not Disappear
items.excerpt: Bloomsbury founder Nigel Newton called the idea that AI will take all publishing jobs 'rubbish'. His panel still agreed that entry-level roles may disappear, staff will need retraining and new roles will emerge.

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Three Views of Innovation
items.excerpt: The CEOs of Sourcebooks, Abrams and Perfect Bound describe using AI in accounting, marketing and production for labor-heavy back-end work. One of them called AI 'the worst thing that has happened to humanity' while still saying publishers must engage with it.

history_match.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Redrawing the Map

items.title: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: English language exports, AI and travel chaos lead conversations
items.excerpt: The Bookseller's Frankfurt wrap says English-language exports, the industry-wide impact of AI, meetings missed to travel chaos, and the new hall layout dominated this year's fair. The body is behind a login wall, so the AI angle is confirmed only from the og:description.

items.title: From Story Seeds To Stories, And Writing An Author's Note, With Joanna Penn
items.excerpt: Joanna Penn argues that when whole stories can be generated from one prompt, an author's note becomes a way to show the human source of a work. The intro also covers the new KDP upload cap and the AI-related Digital Publishing Awards.

items.title: News Podcast: Amazon Cuts KDP Uploads to Two Titles a Week; Study Backs AI Detector Accuracy
items.excerpt: Since September 21, Amazon KDP has allowed two new titles per format per week, down from ten. ALLi reads this as another move against the flood of AI-generated books. The episode also covers a study backing the Pangram AI detector and SCBWI's tougher AI policy.

history_match.title: Amazon KDP limits authors to two titles per format per week

items.title: News Summary: OpenAI Moves to Strike AI Market Study; BISG Survey Shows Indies Use AI Mainly for Marketing
items.excerpt: In the authors' copyright case, OpenAI asked the court to strike Tuhin Chakrabarty's study of generative AI's impact on the book market. Separately, a BISG survey finds indie authors lead the industry in using AI, mainly for marketing.

history_match.title: OpenAI seeks to exclude book market study, citing funding ties to authors' law firm

items.title: Zwischenbilanz der Buchmesse: 65.000 Fachbesucher!
items.excerpt: Frankfurt's interim report counts 65,000 trade visitors in the first two days, level with last year. It says AI dominated the conversation, with CEOs on stage discussing its role; one called AI 'just another storm' the industry will weather.
